messages.content: Please check this: Our science teacher gave us a informations sheet about volcanoes.

Our science teacher gave us an information sheet about volcanoes.
Why: "informations" is uncountable, so no -s; "an" goes before a vowel sound.
Can you correct this? My aunt have two daughters and both of them is studying in Chennai.

My aunt has two daughters and both of them are studying in Chennai.
Why: "aunt" takes "has"; "both of them" takes "are".
What you would like to eat for dinner tonight? Is the word order right?

What would you like to eat for dinner tonight?
Why: a question puts "would" before "you".
We reached at the airport two hours before the flight. Is 'at' needed here?

No, remove it: We reached the airport two hours before the flight.
Why: "reach" takes its object directly, with no "at".
The new manager came in and said us to sit down quietly. What's wrong here?

The new manager came in and told us to sit down quietly.
Why: "tell" takes the person directly; "say" does not.
The shopkeeper gave me a discount, so I paid less money than I had planned. Is this right?

This is already correct.
Why: "money" is uncountable, so "less" is right; "had planned" is fine.
On Raksha Bandhan my sister ties a rakhi on my wrist and give me sweets. Please check.

On Raksha Bandhan my sister ties a rakhi on my wrist and gives me sweets.
Why: "my sister" takes "gives", like "ties".
Our team losed the final but we played good. Correct this, please.

Our team lost the final but we played well.
Why: "lose" becomes "lost"; "played" needs the adverb "well".
The monsoon reach Kerala on early June every year. Fix my sentence.

The monsoon reaches Kerala in early June every year.
Why: "monsoon" takes "reaches"; "in" goes with months.
Three of my favourite book's are on this shelf. What is wrong?

Three of my favourite books are on this shelf.
Why: a plural needs -s only; an apostrophe shows possession.
I felt very embarrassing when everyone laughed at my answer. Is this right?

I felt very embarrassed when everyone laughed at my answer.
Why: "embarrassed" describes the person's feeling; "embarrassing" describes the cause.
Anil and Sunita is my best friend. Please check my sentence.

Anil and Sunita are my best friends.
Why: "Anil and Sunita" is plural: "are" and "friends".
My phone is not working properly, I will buy new one tomorrow. Can you fix it?

My phone is not working properly, so I will buy a new one tomorrow.
Why: a comma cannot join two sentences, so add "so"; "new one" needs "a".
Yesterday was a so cold day that we stayed inside. Correct me.

Yesterday was such a cold day that we stayed inside.
Why: "such" goes before "a + adjective + noun"; "so" goes before an adjective only.
Please keep the books on the shelf and cleaning the table. Is this right?

Please keep the books on the shelf and clean the table.
Why: "and" joins matching forms: "keep" and "clean".
This is the more beautiful song I have ever heard. Check my grammar.

This is the most beautiful song I have ever heard.
Why: one song among all needs "most", not "more".
A cow give milk, and a hen lays egg. Please correct.

A cow gives milk, and a hen lays eggs.
Why: "cow" takes "gives"; general plural "eggs".
The traffic in our city are terrible in the morning. Is the verb right?

The traffic in our city is terrible in the morning.
Why: "traffic" is singular, so "is".
I bought a new shirt, but it doesn't fit to me. What is the mistake?

I bought a new shirt, but it doesn't fit me.
Why: "fit" takes its object directly, with no "to".
My grandfather goes for a walk every morning, and he feels fresh all day. Is this correct?

No change needed.
Why: "goes" and "feels" match "grandfather"; "go for a walk" is normal.
Our office is closed on Sundays, so we works from Monday to Saturday. Please check.

Our office is closed on Sundays, so we work from Monday to Saturday.
Why: "we" takes the base verb "work".
We travelled by the bus to Mysore and returned by the train. What should it be?

We travelled by bus to Mysore and returned by train.
Why: "by bus" and "by train" take no article.
Have you completed your homework yesterday? Fix it please.

Did you complete your homework yesterday?
Why: "yesterday" needs the simple past: "Did you complete".
My grandmother is telling us stories every night when we were young. Can you correct it?

My grandmother used to tell us stories every night when we were young.
Why: a past habit takes "used to", not the present continuous.
I don't eat meat, neither my sister does. Is this right?

I don't eat meat, and neither does my sister.
Why: "neither" puts the helper first: "neither does my sister".
At Christmas, we decorate a small tree and make cards for our neighbours. Is this correct?

Yes, that's right.
Why: "decorate" and "make" fit "we"; "make cards" is the right verb.
We didn't win the trophy, but we did our best. Is this right?

Nothing to fix here.
Why: "do your best" is the fixed phrase; "didn't win" is correct.
The river flows under the bridge in a gentle speed. What's wrong?

The river flows under the bridge at a gentle speed.
Why: speed takes "at": "at a gentle speed".
I borrowed this book to the library last week. Which word is wrong?

I borrowed this book from the library last week.
Why: "borrow" goes with "from"; "to" goes with "lend".
I am afraid of to speak in front of strangers. Please correct.

I am afraid of speaking in front of strangers.
Why: "of" is followed by -ing: "speaking".
Deepa is the person who I can always rely. Fix it please.

Deepa is the person who I can always rely on.
Why: "rely" needs "on", even after "who".
My father pays the electricity bill in the first of every month. Correct this.

My father pays the electricity bill on the first of every month.
Why: dates take "on": "on the first".
The internet connection in our school are very slow today. Is the verb okay?

The internet connection in our school is very slow today.
Why: "connection" is singular, so "is".
A cold wind was blowing and the sky is dark. Please fix the tense.

A cold wind was blowing and the sky was dark.
Why: both parts are in the past: "was".
He cleans the whole house himself, and nobody helps to him. Is this right?

He cleans the whole house himself, and nobody helps him.
Why: "help" takes its object directly, with no "to".
Listening to old songs make me remember my school days. Check this.

Listening to old songs makes me remember my school days.
Why: "Listening to old songs" is singular, so "makes".
The cat jumped onto the shelf and knock down a glass. Fix the verb.

The cat jumped onto the shelf and knocked down a glass.
Why: "jumped" is past, so "knocked" too.
Our city has many old temple and a big market. What is wrong?

Our city has many old temples and a big market.
Why: "many" takes a plural: "temples".
My boss is very polite and never shouts to anyone. Is the preposition correct?

My boss is very polite and never shouts at anyone.
Why: "shout at" means angry; "shout to" means calling out.
My school is nearer to my house than yours is. Is this right?

That sentence is correct.
Why: "nearer" with "than" and "near to" are both right.
Our exam starts from Monday and ends on Friday. Please check.

Our exam starts on Monday and ends on Friday.
Why: a weekday takes "on"; "from" needs "to".
We visited our village for the Holi, and we play with colours. Please correct.

We visited our village for Holi, and we played with colours.
Why: festival names take no article; "visited" needs "played".
We had a very tiring journey, so we slept early. Is this right?

Not quite: We had a very tiring journey, so we went to bed early.
Why: "go to bed early" is standard; "sleep early" is not.
Their was a long queue at the ticket counter. Spelling please.

There was a long queue at the ticket counter.
Why: "there" means exists; "their" means belonging to them.
This wallet is made of leathers. Is that right?

This wallet is made of leather.
Why: "leather" is uncountable, so no -s.
The principle of our school gave the prizes on Annual Day. Which word is wrong?

The principal of our school gave the prizes on Annual Day.
Why: "principal" is the school head; "principle" is a rule.
We walked threw the forest and saw many birds. Check the spelling.

We walked through the forest and saw many birds.
Why: "through" means in and out; "threw" is past of "throw".
I am very happy that you passed, and so is my mother. Is the last part right?

Yes, the last part is right.
Why: "so is my mother" puts the helper before the subject, correctly.
Please inform to the office before you leave early. Fix this.

Please inform the office before you leave early.
Why: "inform" takes its object directly, with no "to".
The childrens' playground is behind the library. Is the apostrophe right?

The children's playground is behind the library.
Why: "children" is already plural, so add 's.
Yesterday I go to the market and met my old teacher. Please correct.

Yesterday I went to the market and met my old teacher.
Why: "yesterday" needs the past tense (went).
I was cooking dinner when the phone was ringing. What should the last verb be?

I was cooking dinner when the phone rang.
Why: a short interrupting action takes the simple past: "rang".
How long are you living in this city? Check my question.

How long have you been living in this city?
Why: "how long" with a continuing action takes "have you been living".
He has been working here from 2018. Is 'from' right?

He has been working here since 2018.
Why: "since" gives the start point; "from" needs an end.
The news about the exam results were shocking. Is the verb right?

The news about the exam results was shocking.
Why: "news" is singular, so "was".
One of my friends are getting married next month. Please check.

One of my friends is getting married next month.
Why: the subject is "one", so "is".
The scissors is on the table in the kitchen. Fix the verb, please.

The scissors are on the table in the kitchen.
Why: "scissors" is plural, so "are".
What is the names of your teachers? Can you correct this question?

What are the names of your teachers?
Why: "names" is plural, so "are".
We watched a film yesterday. Film was very funny. What is missing?

We watched a film yesterday. The film was very funny.
Why: the second mention of the film needs "the".
She is best singer in our school. Correct me.

She is the best singer in our school.
Why: "best" takes "the".
It was a honour to meet your grandfather. Is 'a' right?

It was an honour to meet your grandfather.
Why: "honour" starts with a vowel sound, so "an".
Delhi is capital of India. Is the grammar right?

Delhi is the capital of India.
Why: a unique capital needs "the".
She is interested in painting and good at drawing animals. Is this correct?

Both prepositions are right, so no change is needed.
Why: "interested in" and "good at" are both correct.
I am fond for dancing and singing. Please check.

I am fond of dancing and singing.
Why: "fond" takes "of".
I still depend of my parents for pocket money. What is wrong?

I still depend on my parents for pocket money.
Why: "depend" takes "on".
Please pay attention at the teacher. Which word is wrong?

Please pay attention to the teacher.
Why: the phrase is "pay attention to".
The ball rolled off the table and fell in the floor. Fix the preposition.

The ball rolled off the table and fell on the floor.
Why: a surface takes "on"; "in" means inside.
I always drink tea in the morning. Is 'always' in the right place?

Your word order is fine.
Why: "always" goes after the subject, before the verb.
How you reached here so early? Please fix my question.

How did you reach here so early?
Why: a "how" question needs "did"; the verb goes back to "reach".
I every day walk to school. Is the order okay?

I walk to school every day.
Why: time phrases like "every day" go at the end.
She speaks very well English. Please fix the word order.

She speaks English very well.
Why: the object "English" stays next to the verb.
We bought some new furnitures for the living room. Please correct.

We bought some new furniture for the living room.
Why: "furniture" is uncountable, so no -s.
We saw two deers near the lake. What is wrong?

We saw two deer near the lake.
Why: "deer" is the same in singular and plural.
Several woman in our colony have started a small library. Is it correct?

Several women in our colony have started a small library.
Why: "several" takes a plural: "women".
Our new teacher is less stricter than the old one. Please correct.

Our new teacher is less strict than the old one.
Why: "less" takes the plain adjective, not "stricter".
Of the two sisters, Gita is the oldest. Is that right?

Of the two sisters, Gita is the older.
Why: two people take "older"; "oldest" is for three or more.
He is as tall as his father now. Is this sentence right?

Correct as it stands.
Why: "as tall as" is the correct pattern for equal.
She made the poster by her own. What should it be?

She made the poster on her own.
Why: "on her own" or "by herself"; not "by her own".
He looked at him in the mirror and smiled. Is 'him' right here?

If "him" means the same person as "he", change it to "himself": He looked at himself in the mirror and smiled.
Why: the same person needs "himself".
Is this pen your or mine? Fix my question.

Is this pen yours or mine?
Why: no noun follows, so "yours".
Everyone should bring their own water bottle on the trip. Is 'their' okay here?

Yes, 'their' is fine here.
Why: "their" is normal for "everyone" when gender is unknown.
Can you advice me on which colour to paint the wall? Check my spelling.

Can you advise me on which colour to paint the wall?
Why: "advise" is the verb; "advice" is the noun.
I need to buy some stationary for school tomorrow. Is the word right?

I need to buy some stationery for school tomorrow.
Why: "stationery" is paper and pens; "stationary" is not moving.
The heavy rain had a big affect on the crops. Please correct.

The heavy rain had a big effect on the crops.
Why: "effect" is the noun; "affect" is the verb.
We walked passed the old fort on our way home. Check the spelling.

We walked past the old fort on our way home.
Why: "past" means beyond; "passed" is a verb.
Ravi is tall, his brother is short. What is wrong with the comma?

Ravi is tall, but his brother is short.
Why: a comma cannot join two sentences; add "but".
The dogs bowl is empty, so please fill it. Is there a mistake?

The dog's bowl is empty, so please fill it.
Why: one dog owns it: "dog's".
Its going to be very hot today, so carry water. Please correct.

It's going to be very hot today, so carry water.
Why: "it's" means "it is"; "its" shows possession.
I need to do a phone call before the meeting starts. Is 'do' right?

I need to make a phone call before the meeting starts.
Why: the fixed phrase is "make a phone call".
Let's do a plan for the weekend. What is wrong?

Let's make a plan for the weekend.
Why: we "make" plans.
Please make me a favour and lock the gate. Correct it please.

Please do me a favour and lock the gate.
Why: the fixed phrase is "do someone a favour".
My sister is doing a cake for my birthday. Fix the verb.

My sister is making a cake for my birthday.
Why: "make" is the verb for creating a cake.
The teacher told good morning and we all stood up. Is 'told' right?

The teacher said good morning and we all stood up.
Why: greetings take "said"; "told" needs a person.
It is dark in here, please open the light. Fix this.

It is dark in here, so please switch on the light.
Why: lights are "switched on"; a comma cannot join sentences, so "so".
Please stop to make noise, the baby is sleeping. Correct, please.

Please stop making noise because the baby is sleeping.
Why: "stop" plus -ing means quit; "because" joins the sentences.
I remember to meet him in Pune last year. What is the right form?

I remember meeting him in Pune last year.
Why: "remember" plus -ing is a memory; "remember to" is a duty.
I am thinking to buy a bicycle next month. Please check.

I am thinking of buying a bicycle next month.
Why: "think of" takes -ing.
I want that you come with me to the station. Is this correct English?

I want you to come with me to the station.
Why: "want" takes an object plus "to"; not "that".
My good name is Kiran and I am in class ten. Can you check my introduction?

My name is Kiran and I am in class ten.
Why: "my name" is standard; "good name" is not.
He is my cousin brother and lives in Madurai. Please fix it.

He is my cousin and lives in Madurai.
Why: "cousin" already covers both genders.
I passed out from college in 2020 and joined a firm. Please check this line.

I graduated from college in 2020 and joined a firm.
Why: "pass out" means faint; "graduate from" is right.
Kindly revert back to me by Friday. Is this correct?

Kindly reply to me by Friday.
Why: "revert" means go back; "reply" means answer.
If I was you, I would say sorry to her. Is 'was' right?

If I were you, I would say sorry to her.
Why: an imaginary present takes "were" in careful English.
Neither of my parents are at home right now. Please correct.

Neither of my parents is at home right now.
Why: "neither" means one of two, so "is".
A bunch of keys were found on the bus. What is wrong?

A bunch of keys was found on the bus.
Why: "bunch" is singular, so "was".
She scored a high marks in the science test. Check please.

She scored high marks in the science test.
Why: "marks" is plural, so no "a".
He has few patience, so he gets angry quickly. Fix it.

He has little patience, so he gets angry quickly.
Why: "patience" is uncountable, so "little", not "few".
Suresh is more intelligent than any boy in his class. Is this right?

Suresh is more intelligent than any other boy in his class.
Why: "any other" is needed; Suresh is also a boy in the class.
The more you practise, the better you will play. Is this correct?

Yes, this is already right.
Why: "the more..., the better" is correct; "practise" is correct.
She apologised me for being late. What is missing?

She apologised to me for being late.
Why: "apologise" takes "to" the person.
Please give a call me when you reach home. Fix the order.

Please give me a call when you reach home.
Why: the person comes first: "give me a call".
I will meet you at the libary at four. Check my spelling.

I will meet you at the library at four.
Why: "library" has two r's.
Please recieve the parcel from the postman. Is the spelling right?

Please receive the parcel from the postman.
Why: "i before e, except after c": "receive".
We have a seperate room for guests. What is wrong with the spelling?

We have a separate room for guests.
Why: spell it "separate": "-para-", not "-pera-".
The tourists rode camels across the dessert. Which word is wrong?

The tourists rode camels across the desert.
Why: "desert" is dry land; "dessert" is sweet food.
She wore a lovely dress to the wedding, but it was to big. Please correct.

She wore a lovely dress to the wedding, but it was too big.
Why: "too" means more than enough; "to" does not.
The farmer feeds his cattles twice a day. Is the plural right?

The farmer feeds his cattle twice a day.
Why: "cattle" is already plural, so no -s.
Many peoples came to the fair on Sunday. What should it be?

Many people came to the fair on Sunday.
Why: "people" is already plural; "peoples" means nations.
I wanted to go, however it was raining. Please correct the punctuation.

I wanted to go; however, it was raining.
Why: "however" needs a semicolon before it and a comma after.
I lost the bus, so I walked to the office. Is 'lost' right?

I missed the bus, so I walked to the office.
Why: you "miss" a bus; "lose" is for things.
I will give the exam tomorrow. Please check my sentence.

I will take the exam tomorrow.
Why: a student "takes" an exam.
He spoke a lie about the broken vase. Fix it.

He told a lie about the broken vase.
Why: the fixed phrase is "tell a lie".
I go to the market for buying vegetables every Sunday. Is it correct?

I go to the market to buy vegetables every Sunday.
Why: purpose takes "to" plus the base verb.
He decided going to Mumbai after college. Please correct.

He decided to go to Mumbai after college.
Why: "decide" takes "to" plus the base verb.
He is capable to do this job alone. What is wrong?

He is capable of doing this job alone.
Why: "capable" takes "of" plus -ing.
A new girl joined our class. She's name is Pooja. Please check.

A new girl joined our class. Her name is Pooja.
Why: "she's" means "she is"; "her" shows possession.
I met the boy who bicycle was stolen. Which word is wrong?

I met the boy whose bicycle was stolen.
Why: "whose" shows ownership; "who" is a subject.
She is the girl which won the prize. Is 'which' right?

She is the girl who won the prize.
Why: "who" is for people; "which" is for things.
I have been waiting here for an hour, and the bus has not come yet. Is this correct?

It is right as it is.
Why: "have been waiting" and "has not come yet" are correct.
She plays violin beautifully. What is missing?

She plays the violin beautifully.
Why: "play the" goes before an instrument.
What a nice weather we are having today! Please correct.

What nice weather we are having today!
Why: "weather" is uncountable, so no "a".
She has a long black hair. Is it right?

She has long black hair.
Why: "hair" is uncountable, so no "a".
I want to be pilot when I grow up. Please correct.

I want to be a pilot when I grow up.
Why: a singular job title needs "a".
The bus had left before I reach the stop. Fix the tense.

The bus had left before I reached the stop.
Why: the later event takes the simple past: "reached".
The tea is not enough hot. Please fix the order.

The tea is not hot enough.
Why: "enough" goes after an adjective.
She sings so well that everyone stops to listen. Is this right?

That is correct; nothing to change.
Why: "so + adverb + that" is correct; "stops to listen" is correct.
I am late because of the lift was broken. Is 'because of' right?

I am late because the lift was broken.
Why: "because of" takes a noun; "because" takes a clause.
I called him yesterday night, but he did not answer. Please check.

I called him last night, but he did not answer.
Why: "last night" is standard; "yesterday night" is not.
You are coming to the party tomorrow, isn't it? Is the end right?

You are coming to the party tomorrow, aren't you?
Why: the tag repeats the helper verb: "aren't you".
It is late. Let's go to home now. What is wrong?

It is late. Let's go home now.
Why: "home" is an adverb, so no "to".
I walk for an hour everyday after dinner. Is 'everyday' right?

I walk for an hour every day after dinner.
Why: "every day" is two words as a time adverb.
I like mangoes alot. Please check the spelling.

I like mangoes a lot.
Why: "a lot" is two words.
I will definately visit you in Pune. Spelling, please.

I will definitely visit you in Pune.
Why: spell it "definitely", with "-ite-".
The final match is on Wensday. Check my spelling.

The final match is on Wednesday.
Why: "Wednesday" has a silent d: Wed-nes-day.
Their going to arrive by noon. Is it correct?

They're going to arrive by noon.
Why: "they're" means "they are"; "their" shows possession.
I saved enough pocket money to buy a new bat. Is this right?

This sentence is fine as written.
Why: "enough" goes before a noun; "to buy" gives the purpose.
The parrot repeated everything we said, and it made us laugh. Is this right?

No mistake here; it is correct.
Why: "made us laugh" takes the base verb without "to".
My uncle learned me how to ride a bicycle. Please correct.

My uncle taught me how to ride a bicycle.
Why: "teach" gives knowledge; "learn" gets it.
My phone's battery got finished so I could not call you. Please fix.

My phone's battery ran out, so I could not call you.
Why: the phrase is "ran out"; "so" needs a comma before it.
She is not feeling well, so she is taking rest at home. Is the last part right?

She is not feeling well, so she is resting at home.
Why: "rest" works as the verb "resting"; "taking rest" needs "a".
At dusk we lit candles along the steps, and the house looked lovely. Is this right?

Yes, you wrote it correctly.
Why: "lit" is the past of "light"; "looked" takes an adjective.
I am not understanding this chapter. Can you explain it?

I do not understand this chapter. Can you explain it?
Why: "understand" is a stative verb, so no continuous.
I am waiting for this bus for half an hour. What is wrong?

I have been waiting for this bus for half an hour.
Why: an action still continuing takes "have been waiting".
It is the first time I eat this sweet. Please check my tense.

It is the first time I have eaten this sweet.
Why: "the first time" takes the present perfect: "have eaten".
The number of students in our club are increasing. Is the verb right?

The number of students in our club is increasing.
Why: "the number of" is singular, so "is".
Where is my sandals? I left them here. Please correct my question.

Where are my sandals? I left them here.
Why: "sandals" is plural, so "are".
Half of the cake were eaten before the guests arrived. Fix it.

Half of the cake was eaten before the guests arrived.
Why: the verb follows "cake", which is singular: "was".
The Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world. What should I change?

Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
Why: a single mountain name takes no "the".
We visited Taj Mahal on our school trip. Is an article missing?

We visited the Taj Mahal on our school trip.
Why: famous monuments usually take "the".
Moon is shining brightly tonight. Please correct.

The moon is shining brightly tonight.
Why: there is one moon, so "the".
We congratulated Dev on his success in the quiz. Is this correct?

Yes, "on" is the right word.
Why: "congratulate" takes "on", so "on" is right.
She is very proud for her daughter. Which word is wrong?

She is very proud of her daughter.
Why: "proud" takes "of".
Don't laugh on other people's mistakes. Fix the preposition.

Don't laugh at other people's mistakes.
Why: "laugh at" is the phrase.
He was absent in class yesterday. Is 'in' right?

He was absent from class yesterday.
Why: "absent" takes "from".
The mango was full with juice. Please check.

The mango was full of juice.
Why: "full" takes "of".
I have no interest on sports. What is wrong?

I have no interest in sports.
Why: "interest" takes "in".
The bus arrived to the village at night. Correct the preposition.

The bus arrived at the village at night.
Why: "arrive" takes "at" or "in", never "to".
Who you are waiting for? Correct my question.

Who are you waiting for?
Why: a question puts "are" before "you".
What means this word? Please fix my question.

What does this word mean?
Why: a question needs "does"; the verb goes back to "mean".
Could you tell me where the post office is? Is this correct?

This is already well formed.
Why: an indirect question keeps statement order, so it is right.
I have two sister-in-laws in Pune. Is the plural right?

I have two sisters-in-law in Pune.
Why: in compounds the main noun takes the plural: "sisters-in-law".
The tomatos are cheap at the market today. Check the spelling.

The tomatoes are cheap at the market today.
Why: nouns ending in consonant plus -o often take -es: "tomatoes".
Five thousands people came to the fair. Please correct.

Five thousand people came to the fair.
Why: "thousand" stays singular after a number.
I have many works to finish before the weekend. What is wrong?

I have a lot of work to finish before the weekend.
Why: "work" is uncountable, so "a lot of work", not "many works".
Of all my cousins, Rhea is the funniest. Is this right?

Yes, "the funniest" is correct.
Why: "the funniest" is correct for one person in a group.
The weather today is better than yesterday. Is the comparison right?

The weather today is better than yesterday's.
Why: compare like with like: "yesterday's" (weather).
My friend and myself went to the fair. Fix it, please.

He read the poem allowed to the whole class. Is "allowed" the right word?

He read the poem aloud to the whole class.
Why: "Aloud" means out loud; "allowed" means permitted.
A polar bare walked across the ice in the video. Which word is wrong?

A polar bear walked across the ice in the video.
Why: "Bear" is the animal; "bare" means uncovered.
Please don't waist water while washing the car. Check the spelling.

Please don't waste water while washing the car.
Why: "Waste" means misuse; "waist" is a body part.
She said "I am tired and want to rest". Please fix the punctuation.

She said, "I am tired and want to rest."
Why: A comma introduces speech; the full stop goes inside the quotes.
I like tea; but my brother likes coffee. Is the semicolon right?

I like tea, but my brother likes coffee.
Why: "But" takes a comma, not a semicolon.
Because it was raining, we stayed home and played cards. Do I need a comma after "raining"?

Yes, your comma is right.
Why: A comma follows an opening "because" clause.
Can we prepone the meeting to Thursday? Is "prepone" a real word?

Yes, it is a real word in Indian English, but many readers elsewhere do not know it. A version that works everywhere: Can we bring the meeting forward to Thursday?
Why: "Prepone" is Indian English; "bring forward" is standard.
The bank is opposite to the school on this road. Is "opposite to" okay?

The bank is opposite the school on this road.
Why: "Opposite to" is common in India; "opposite" alone is standard.
Walking to school, a dog chased me. Does the opening phrase work?

Walking to school, I was chased by a dog.
Why: The opening phrase must describe the subject, so "I" is subject.
I bought a cake for my mother with chocolate icing. Is the order of the words clear?

I bought a cake with chocolate icing for my mother.
Why: Keep "with chocolate icing" next to "cake".
The boy was hit by a ball wearing a red cap. Something sounds odd to me.

The boy wearing a red cap was hit by a ball.
Why: Keep "wearing a red cap" next to "the boy".
Covered in dust, I cleaned the old bookshelf. Does that describe the right thing?

I cleaned the old bookshelf, which was covered in dust.
Why: The opening phrase would describe "I"; use a clause for the bookshelf.
I couldn't find my ticket nowhere in the bag. What is wrong?

I couldn't find my ticket anywhere in the bag.
Why: "Couldn't" plus "nowhere" is a double negative; use "anywhere".
She hardly never misses a class. Is "hardly never" right?

She hardly ever misses a class.
Why: "Hardly" is already negative; say "hardly ever".
She likes coffee, isn't she? Please check the tag.

She likes coffee, doesn't she?
Why: The tag repeats the helper: present simple needs "doesn't".
I am late, amn't I? Is "amn't I" correct?

I am late, aren't I?
Why: "Aren't I?" is the standard tag; "amn't" is dialect.
You won't tell anyone about this, will you? Is the tag right after "won't"?

Yes, the tag is right.
Why: After a negative statement, the tag is positive.
It is a long time that I saw you. How can I say this more naturally?

It has been a long time since I saw you.
Why: "It has been a long time since" plus past simple is standard.
I have not met my uncle since long. Is "since long" okay?

I have not met my uncle for a long time.
Why: "Since" needs a starting point; use "for a long time".
My friend did friendship with a new girl in class. Which verb is wrong?

My friend made friends with a new girl in class.
Why: The phrase is "make friends"; "do" does not fit.
She makes exercise at the park every evening. Please correct the verb.

She does exercise at the park every evening.
Why: "Exercise" takes "do", not "make".
I make a walk along the river after dinner. Is "make a walk" right?

I take a walk along the river after dinner.
Why: The phrase is "take a walk".
We made an experiment to see which cloth dries faster. Which verb is right?

We did an experiment to see which cloth dries faster.
Why: Experiments are "done", not "made".
She is keen in learning the veena. Is "keen in" correct?

She is keen on learning the veena.
Why: "Keen" takes "on".
He is responsible of the school library this year. Which preposition fits?

He is responsible for the school library this year.
Why: "Responsible" takes "for".
She succeeded to win the gold medal after years of practice. Check the verb pattern.

She succeeded in winning the gold medal after years of practice.
Why: "Succeed in" takes -ing.
I am not familiar to this area, so please guide me. Is "familiar to" okay?

I am not familiar with this area, so please guide me.
Why: A person is "familiar with" a place.
I will get my phone to repair tomorrow. What is the right pattern?

I will get my phone repaired tomorrow.
Why: "Get" plus object plus participle: "get my phone repaired".
I had my bicycle repaired yesterday. Is "had my bicycle repaired" correct?

This is already correct.
Why: "Have" plus object plus participle is correct.
The bridge is been repaired this month. Please fix the verb.

The bridge is being repaired this month.
Why: Present continuous passive is "is being" plus participle.
Please pick up him at the station at six. Is the word order right?

Please pick him up at the station at six.
Why: A pronoun object goes between verb and particle: "pick him up".
Where are you going today. Check my end punctuation.

Where are you going today?
Why: A direct question ends with a question mark.
She is a well known writer in our town. Does "well known" need a hyphen?

She is a well-known writer in our town.
Why: A compound adjective before a noun takes a hyphen.
My uncle is twenty five years older than my aunt. Is there a punctuation problem?

My uncle is twenty-five years older than my aunt.
Why: Numbers 21 to 99 take a hyphen.
My cousin is of sixteen years and plays tennis. How do I say the age correctly?

My cousin is sixteen years old and plays tennis.
Why: "Sixteen years old" is standard; "is of sixteen years" is Indian English.
Yesterday I met with an accident near the bus stand, but I am fine. Please correct.

Yesterday I had an accident near the bus stand, but I am fine.
Why: "Have an accident" is standard; "meet with" is Indian English.
How is the weather like in Shimla now? What is wrong with the question?

What is the weather like in Shimla now?
Why: "What...like" asks for description; "how" and "like" don't combine.
Remember to take your notebook when you come to my house tomorrow. Is "take" right?

Remember to bring your notebook when you come to my house tomorrow.
Why: "Bring" means toward the speaker; "take" means away.
This is an economic way to travel to the city. Is "economic" the word I want?

This is an economical way to travel to the city.
Why: "Economical" means saving money; "economic" is about the economy.
She is very sensible about other people's feelings. Is "sensible" right?

She is very sensitive to other people's feelings.
Why: "Sensitive" notices feelings; "sensible" means practical.
The mens' hockey team won the district cup. Where does the apostrophe go?

The men's hockey team won the district cup.
Why: "Men" is already plural, so add 's.
She likes cooking, to read and playing chess. Fix the list.

She likes cooking, reading and playing chess.
Why: List items need the same form (-ing).
Please repeat that again, I could not hear you. Is "repeat again" needed?

Please repeat that. I could not hear you.
Why: "Repeat" already means "say again"; split the two sentences.
My sister works like a nurse in Pune. Is "like" right here?

My sister works as a nurse in Pune.
Why: "As" is for a job; "like" means similar to.
Ravi is a friend of my from school. Please fix the end.

Ravi is a friend of mine from school.
Why: After "of", use "mine".
She walked in to the kitchen and opened the fridge. Is "in to" two words?

She walked into the kitchen and opened the fridge.
Why: "Into" is one word for movement inside.
Lets meet at the bus stop at five. Fix the apostrophe, please.

Let's meet at the bus stop at five.
Why: "Let's" means "let us" and needs an apostrophe.
She lead the team to victory in last year's final. Is "lead" right?

She led the team to victory in last year's final.
Why: The past of "lead" is "led".
I like to wonder around the old market on Sunday mornings. Which word is wrong?

I like to wander around the old market on Sunday mornings.
Why: "Wander" means walk around; "wonder" means think.
My brother eats serial with milk every morning. Is the spelling right?

My brother eats cereal with milk every morning.
Why: "Cereal" is the food; "serial" means in a series.
The new bridge is made of steal and concrete. Check the spelling.

The new bridge is made of steel and concrete.
Why: "Steel" is the metal; "steal" means take.
Whom did you invite to the party? Should it be "who" instead?

No, "whom" is correct in careful English.
Why: "Whom" is the object of "invite"; "who" is casual.
She doesn't have any brothers or sisters. Is there a double negative here?

No, the sentence is correct.
Why: Only "doesn't" is negative, and "any" suits it.
If I have time, I would visit you on Sunday. Please check the conditional.

If I have time, I will visit you on Sunday.
Why: Real future takes present in "if" and "will" in the main clause.
Those who is late must wait outside the hall. Which verb is right?

Those who are late must wait outside the hall.
Why: "Those" is plural, so "who" takes "are".
Neither Raj nor I am going to the fair. Does the verb agree with "I"?

Yes, "am" is correct.
Why: With "neither...nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject (am).
The all students were happy about the holiday. What should change?

All the students were happy about the holiday.
Why: "All" comes before "the".
We stayed in instead of to go out in the rain. Please correct the end.

We stayed in instead of going out in the rain.
Why: After "instead of", use -ing.
The food was cheap. In the other hand, the service was slow. Check the phrase.

The food was cheap. On the other hand, the service was slow.
Why: The fixed phrase is "on the other hand".
In my point of view, school uniforms are very useful. Is "in my point of view" right?

From my point of view, school uniforms are very useful.
Why: "From my point of view" or "in my view" is the usual phrase.
In the end of the film, everybody clapped. Which words are wrong?

At the end of the film, everybody clapped.
Why: "At the end of" takes a noun; "in the end" stands alone.
According to me, the exam was easy. Is "according to me" okay?

In my opinion, the exam was easy.
Why: "According to" names another source; "in my opinion" fits better.
The teacher emphasised on neat handwriting in all subjects. What should I change?

The teacher emphasised neat handwriting in all subjects.
Why: "Emphasise" takes no "on".
All parents must attend to the meeting on Friday. Is "attend to" right?

All parents must attend the meeting on Friday.
Why: "Attend" an event takes no "to".
In case it will rain, take an umbrella. Please check the verb.

In case it rains, take an umbrella.
Why: After "in case", use the present, not "will".
When I was small, I would be afraid of dogs. Is "would be" right?

When I was small, I was afraid of dogs.
Why: "Would" is for repeated actions; use the simple past for a state.
I use to walk to school when I was small. What is wrong?

I used to walk to school when I was small.
Why: The phrase is "used to", with a "d".
She is doing a MBA in Pune after working for two years. Is the article right?

She is doing an MBA in Pune after working for two years.
Why: "MBA" starts with a vowel sound, so "an".
Once upon time there lived a clever crow in a banyan tree. What is missing?

Once upon a time there lived a clever crow in a banyan tree.
Why: The fixed phrase is "once upon a time".
Every night I go to the bed at ten and wake up at six. Is "the bed" right?

Every night I go to bed at ten and wake up at six.
Why: "Go to bed" takes no article.
He studies hardly before exams, so he always does well. Is "hardly" the right word?

He studies hard before exams, so he always does well.
Why: "Hard" is the adverb; "hardly" means almost not.
She arrived lately at the station, and the train had gone. Which word is wrong?

She arrived late at the station, and the train had gone.
Why: "Late" means after the expected time; "lately" means recently.
The kite flew highly above the terrace and then dipped. Check the adverb.

The kite flew high above the terrace and then dipped.
Why: "High" is the adverb for height; "highly" means very much.
I am very tired to cook tonight. Can you fix the pattern?

I am too tired to cook tonight.
Why: "Too" plus adjective plus "to" shows something prevents the action.
Because the road was closed, so we took another route. What is wrong?

Because the road was closed, we took another route.
Why: "Because" and "so" both show cause; use only one.
I did not go to the park. Because I was tired. Is the second part a sentence?

I did not go to the park because I was tired.
Why: A "because" clause cannot stand alone; join it.
A large amount of students joined the drama club this year. Which word is wrong?

A large number of students joined the drama club this year.
Why: "Number" goes with countable nouns, "amount" with uncountable.
The sweets were divided between the five children. Is "between" the right word?

The sweets were divided among the five children.
Why: "Among" is for more than two.
The programme starts at 6 pm in the evening. Is something repeated?

The programme starts at 6 pm.
Why: "Pm" already shows evening, so "in the evening" repeats.
Is very cold in the hills in December, so we pack warm clothes. What is missing?

It is very cold in the hills in December, so we pack warm clothes.
Why: A sentence needs a subject; weather takes "it".
It has a small library in our village now. Is "it has" right?

There is a small library in our village now.
Why: To say something exists, use "there is".
Please remember me to call Aunt Rita on Sunday. Is "remember me" right?

Please remind me to call Aunt Rita on Sunday.
Why: "Remind" helps another remember; "remember" is your own memory.
I knew your sister at the fair yesterday. Is "knew" right for a first meeting?

I met your sister at the fair yesterday.
Why: "Know" is a state; a first meeting takes "met".
She paid the tickets by card at the counter. Is something missing?

She paid for the tickets by card at the counter.
Why: Use "pay for" for the thing you buy.
She is putting a green saree today and looks lovely. Is "putting" the right verb?

She is wearing a green saree today and looks lovely.
Why: "Wear" is what you have on; "put on" is the action.
My sister participated to the quiz and came second. Which preposition is right?

My sister participated in the quiz and came second.
Why: The phrase is "participate in".
She cannot concentrate in her work when the music is loud. Which preposition is right?

She cannot concentrate on her work when the music is loud.
Why: "Concentrate" takes "on".
I am not sure whether she will come or no. How do I fix the end?

I am not sure whether she will come or not.
Why: The fixed pair is "whether...or not".
Almost people in our street keep a pet. Which word is wrong?

Most people in our street keep a pet.
Why: "Most" works before a noun; "almost" is an adverb.
How about to visit the museum on Saturday? Is "how about to" right?

How about visiting the museum on Saturday?
Why: "How about" takes -ing.
No sooner did he sit down when the bell rang. Something is wrong with the pair of words.

No sooner did he sit down than the bell rang.
Why: "No sooner" pairs with "than".
Do you have a time to talk about the schedule? What is off?

Do you have time to talk about the schedule?
Why: "Time" meaning free time is uncountable; drop "a".
I am sorry for late, the bus broke down on the way. Please correct.

I am sorry for being late. The bus broke down on the way.
Why: "Sorry for" takes -ing (being late); split the sentences.
Thank you for your helping me with the project. Is "your helping" right?

Thank you for helping me with the project.
Why: "Thank you for" takes -ing or a noun, not both.
Do you know to swim? How do I ask this properly?

Do you know how to swim?
Why: A skill needs "know how to".
See you on tomorrow at the bus stop. Is "on" needed?

See you tomorrow at the bus stop.
Why: "Tomorrow" takes no preposition; "on tomorrow" is Indian English.
I admire her patient with young children. Which word should change?

I admire her patience with young children.
Why: After "her", use the noun "patience".
What is the different between a lake and a pond? Is the word right?

What is the difference between a lake and a pond?
Why: "The" needs a noun: "difference".
Please keep the door close so the cat cannot get out. Which word is wrong?

Please keep the door closed so the cat cannot get out.
Why: Use the participle "closed" for the door's state.
How long is your school from here? Is "how long" right?

How far is your school from here?
Why: "How far" asks distance; "how long" asks time.
I'm going to the market; do you need anything? Can I use a semicolon here?

It is acceptable.
Why: A semicolon can join two linked sentences; a full stop works too.
I shall be happy to help you with the form. Is "shall" too old-fashioned?

It is correct, and it sounds polite.
Why: "Shall" with "I" is correct and polite; "will" is common.
Anyone who wants a seat should raise their hand. Should it be "his or her" instead of "their"?

Both are acceptable, so no change is needed.
Why: Singular "their" is widely accepted; "his or her" is more formal.
There is some bread and two eggs on the plate. Should it be "are" because of the eggs?

No, "is" is acceptable here.
Why: After "there", the verb agrees with the first item; "are" is common too.
Had I known about the delay, I would have left earlier. Is it okay to start with "Had I known"?

Yes, it is correct.
Why: "Had I known" is a formal "If I had known".
I look forward to seeing you next week. Should it be "to see"?

No, "seeing" is right.
Why: "To" in "look forward to" is a preposition, so -ing.
If I were you, I would apologise to her. Is "were" correct with "I"?

Yes, "were" is correct here.
Why: An unreal condition uses "were"; "was" is casual.
Mum and Dad are coming to my school's Annual Day. Do "Mum" and "Dad" need capitals here?

Yes, the capitals are correct.
Why: Family words used as names take capitals.
The Himalayas is the highest mountain range in the world. Is the verb okay?

The Himalayas are the highest mountain range in the world.
Why: "Himalayas" is plural, so "are".
I have met your cousin two years ago at Neha's wedding. Which tense should I use?

I met your cousin two years ago at Neha's wedding.
Why: "Two years ago" needs the past simple.
I am very exciting about the science fair next week. Can you correct it?

I am very excited about the science fair next week.
Why: "Excited" is the feeling; "exciting" is the cause.
My brother didn't came home for lunch today. What is the mistake?

My brother didn't come home for lunch today.
Why: After "didn't", the verb is base form (come).
Do you can play the flute? Please fix my question.

Can you play the flute?
Why: "Can" forms questions by moving before the subject, not with "do".
This steel tiffin box belongs for my grandfather. Which word is wrong?

This steel tiffin box belongs to my grandfather.
Why: "Belong" takes "to".
I like to listen the radio while I cook dinner. Please correct this.

I like to listen to the radio while I cook dinner.
Why: "Listen" takes "to".
My neighbour has been suffering with fever for three days now. Is "with" okay?

My neighbour has been suffering from fever for three days now.
Why: "Suffer" takes "from".
She applied to the receptionist job at the clinic last week. Fix the preposition.

She applied for the receptionist job at the clinic last week.
Why: Apply "for" a job.
My grandmother believes on the power of prayer. Please check.

My grandmother believes in the power of prayer.
Why: The pattern is "believe in".
The guard was accused for stealing a bicycle, but he was innocent. What should it be?

The guard was accused of stealing a bicycle, but he was innocent.
Why: "Accuse" takes "of".
I thank to you for helping me with the luggage. Is this right?

I thank you for helping me with the luggage.
Why: "Thank" takes the person directly, no "to".
She has lack of confidence in maths, but she is improving. Is something missing?

She has a lack of confidence in maths, but she is improving.
Why: The noun "lack" needs "a" before it.
My shirt is same like yours, but mine is bigger. Please correct it.

My shirt is the same as yours, but mine is bigger.
Why: "The same" takes "as", not "like".
The new bypass is more better than the old road. Fix this, please.

The new bypass is better than the old road.
Why: "Better" is already comparative; drop "more".
Today's heat is much more worse than yesterday's. What is wrong?

Today's heat is much worse than yesterday's.
Why: "Worse" is already comparative; drop "more".
This brand of cotton is superior than that one. Is "than" right?

This brand of cotton is superior to that one.
Why: "Superior" takes "to", not "than".
Let's look the cricket final at my house tonight. Which verb is better?

Let's watch the cricket final at my house tonight.
Why: For a match, use "watch", not "look".
I am liking this song very much. Can you simplify the verb?

I like this song very much.
Why: "Like" is a state verb; no continuous.
Rarely he eats food from outside. Is the order right?

Rarely does he eat food from outside.
Why: After "rarely" at the start, the helper comes first (does he eat).
Which one you want, the red pen or the blue pen? Please fix the question.

Which one do you want, the red pen or the blue pen?
Why: A question needs "do" before the subject.
My mother sang all the day while she cleaned the house. Is "the" needed?

My mother sang all day while she cleaned the house.
Why: The phrase is "all day", no "the".
None of the boys have finished the quiz yet. Is "have" okay with "none"?

This is acceptable as written.
Why: "None" takes a singular or plural verb; "have" is common.
I like to eat the fruits in the morning. Is "the" needed?

I like to eat fruits in the morning.
Why: Food in general takes no article.
We saw a peacock who was dancing near the pond. Is "who" right for a bird?

We saw a peacock that was dancing near the pond.
Why: Use "that" for animals; "who" is for people.
Feed your pet regular, and it will stay happy. What is the right word?

Feed your pet regularly, and it will stay happy.
Why: "Feed" needs an adverb (regularly).
We exchanged sweets and good wishes with our neighbours at Diwali. Is this correct?

No change needed.
Why: Past simple, "at" for festivals, and "exchange...with" are all right.
I am worried for my sister's result. What should the preposition be?

I am worried about my sister's result.
Why: "Worried" takes "about".
I read the novel twice and then I lend it to my friend. Please check the verb.

I read the novel twice and then I lent it to my friend.
Why: The story is past, and the past of "lend" is "lent".
The metro in our city is very clean and quick, and it saves a lot of times. Fix please.

The metro in our city is very clean and quick, and it saves a lot of time.
Why: "Time" is uncountable here; no plural.
We went to a trip to Munnar last December. Which word is wrong?

We went on a trip to Munnar last December.
Why: The phrase is "go on a trip".
The train from Chennai will arrive on 6:30 in the evening. Please correct.

The train from Chennai will arrive at 6:30 in the evening.
Why: Use "at" with clock times.
Please take care about your bag in the crowd. Fix the phrase.

Please take care of your bag in the crowd.
Why: The phrase is "take care of".
Kindly do the needful and send the form by tomorrow. Is "do the needful" correct?

It is fine in Indian English as written.
Why: "Do the needful" is Indian business English; "please send" is neutral.
After exercise, I feel more energetic and relax. Please fix the last word.

After exercise, I feel more energetic and relaxed.
Why: "Relax" is a verb; "relaxed" matches "energetic".
My grandfather has gone for a checkup, and he will back soon. What is missing?

My grandfather has gone for a checkup, and he will be back soon.
Why: "Will" needs a verb, so "be" is missing.
I owe my cousin two hundred rupees, and I will pay him back on Saturday. Anything to fix?

No, it is already correct.
Why: "Owe", "pay him back" and "on Saturday" are all right.
The school fees was increased this year. What is wrong?

The school fees were increased this year.
Why: "Fees" is plural, so "were".
Tanvi ran so fast that she beat all the other runners and win the race. Fix the last verb.

Tanvi ran so fast that she beat all the other runners and won the race.
Why: The story is past, so "won".
She catched the ball with one hand and the crowd cheered. What is the right form?

She caught the ball with one hand and the crowd cheered.
Why: "Catch" is irregular; the past is "caught".
I might can join the chess club next month. Is this okay?

I might be able to join the chess club next month.
Why: Two modals don't combine; use "be able to".
We climbed up the hill till the top and sat under a tree. Is "till" right?

We climbed up the hill to the top and sat under a tree.
Why: "To" is used for places; "till" is for time.
Our dog is very friendly with stranger and loves children. What is wrong?

Our dog is very friendly with strangers and loves children.
Why: Speaking generally needs the plural "strangers".
The video was so long that I felt asleep halfway. Which word is wrong?

The video was so long that I fell asleep halfway.
Why: The phrase is "fall asleep"; the past is "fell".
Is the Wi-Fi working? I can't connect to it. Can you check this short message?

Yes, that's right as it stands.
Why: Both sentences are complete; "connect to" is right.
I was late to school because the bus got stuck in traffic. Please correct it.

I was late for school because the bus got stuck in traffic.
Why: The phrase is "late for".
There is a pharmacy, a bakery, and a post office on this street. Is the list punctuated right?

This is already correct.
Why: The comma before "and" in a list is optional.
The artist mixed blue and yellow to make a green. Is "a" needed?

The artist mixed blue and yellow to make green.
Why: A colour named in general takes no article.
The museum has a lots of old paintings and statues. What should I change?

The museum has a lot of old paintings and statues.
Why: The phrase is "a lot of", not "a lots of".
Wash your hands before to eat. What is wrong with this?

Wash your hands before eating.
Why: After "before", the verb takes -ing.
The boy who won the race, got a medal from the chief guest. Is the comma needed?

The boy who won the race got a medal from the chief guest.
Why: No comma between the subject and its verb.
i think i left my geometry box in the classroom. What should I fix?

I think I left my geometry box in the classroom.
Why: "I" and the first word of a sentence take capitals.
My cousin speaks english and hindi, and she is learning tamil. Please check the capitals.

My cousin speaks English and Hindi, and she is learning Tamil.
Why: Language names take capitals.
Cut the apple into two halfs and share it with your sister. Is "halfs" right?

Cut the apple into two halves and share it with your sister.
Why: "Half" becomes "halves".
Cats are said to have nine lifes. Please check the plural.

Cats are said to have nine lives.
Why: "Life" becomes "lives".
My foots are cold when I walk on the wet grass. What is wrong?

My feet are cold when I walk on the wet grass.
Why: "Foot" has the irregular plural "feet".
Two thiefs were caught near the station last night. Is the plural correct?

Two thieves were caught near the station last night.
Why: "Thief" becomes "thieves".
I washed my cloths and hung them on the balcony. Is that the right word?

I washed my clothes and hung them on the balcony.
Why: "Cloths" are fabric pieces; wearables are "clothes".
Lightening flashed across the sky, and then the thunder rolled. Check the first word.

Lightning flashed across the sky, and then the thunder rolled.
Why: The sky flash is "lightning"; "lightening" means making lighter.
She bought her lunch from home in a steel box. Which verb is right?
